title: Backup and Archiving
description: Learn about AWS Backup, S3 Glacier, Glacier Deep Archive, and backup vaults.

data.text: Data protection is essential for any business. AWS offers backup and archiving services that help you protect your data from accidental deletion, hardware failure, and disasters. AWS Backup centralizes backup management, while S3 Glacier and Glacier Deep Archive provide long-term archival at the lowest cost.

data.title: Backups Are Not Optional
data.text: Even with highly durable storage like S3 (11 nines of durability), backups are still important. Human error, ransomware, and application bugs can delete data faster than hardware failures. Always follow the 3-2-1 backup rule.

AWS Backup is a fully managed service that centralizes and automates backup across AWS services. It supports EBS, EFS, FSx, DynamoDB, RDS, and more. You define backup plans that specify frequency, retention, and backup vaults. AWS Backup then automatically executes the plan and manages the lifecycle.
S3 Glacier and Glacier Deep Archive

S3 Glacier is an archival storage class designed for data that is rarely accessed and must be retained for years. There are three tiers: Glacier Instant Retrieval for millisecond access, Glacier Flexible Retrieval for minutes-to-hours access, and Glacier Deep Archive for the lowest cost with hours-to-days retrieval time.

Backup vaults are containers that store your backups. AWS Backup uses backup vaults to organize and secure your backup data. You can apply AWS Key Management Service (KMS) keys to vaults to encrypt backups, and you can set up access policies to control who can access backup data.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: AWS Backup centralizes backup management across multiple AWS services
Backup plans define when and how long to retain backups
Backup vaults provide secure, encrypted storage for backups
S3 Glacier offers three archival tiers for different access patterns
Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest option for long-term compliance archives
